newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel tells Egypt settlements in line with peace.
newsitem.headline: Israel tells Egypt settlements in line with peace.

text.p: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Friday that he had sent a letter to Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak defending Israel's settlement policy in the West Bank and Gaza Strip.
Asked by Israel Television if Mubarak had warned him the establishment of new Jewish settlements would harm Israel's peace accord with Egypt, Netanyahu said:
"I received a message, a letter from President Mubarak. I sent him a letter in return. In his letter he really expressed their concern over our settlement policy.
"There was no threat but I can say that I clarified to President Mubarak that our policy on our right to settle and to build the existing settlements is a policy that is in line with peace."

The Egyptian government daily newspaper al-Ahram said on Friday Mubarak sent an "urgent message" to Netanyahu to warn him that new settlement activity on occupied Arab land threatens the Jewish state's peace agreements with its neighbours.
Netanyahu, elected in May, has enraged Arabs with his decision to lift a freeze on settlement building imposed by the Jewish state's former Labour government
He paid his first official visit to a Jewish settlement in the West Bank on Tuesday in a show of defiance to Palestinians opposed to his settlement policy.

Settlements, where more than 130,000 Jews live amid nearly two million Palestinians in the West Bank and Gaza Strip, were left for final status talks by an interim peace deal signed by Israel's previous government and the PLO in September 1993.
Egypt was the first Arab state to sign a peace treaty with Israel in 1979. The Arab League has called an emergency meeting in Cairo on Sunday to discuss Israel's expansion of settlements.
